phase3_findings.description: Bounded 30-char window returns the number on a genuinely-outbound free-prose line whose number sits past the window (e.g. 'Blocks the release train ... #10') — a reverse-axis residual the shipped broad rule lacked; worst for the persistent native stamp.
Same far-separated-outbound residual; the fabricated blocker is emitted with no stderr breadcrumb (silent).
issue-template sentence's absolute 'no longer alters or suppresses the declaration' is contradicted by a reason that writes an ordering word adjacent to its own number.
No upper-bound test for _OUTBOUND_WINDOW; no far-separated-outbound residual test; no template mixed-number edge test.

fix_decisions.claim_text: bounded window introduces a false BLOCKED on far-separated outbound free-prose lines
fix_decisions.evidence: Real and corroborated, but it is the inherent cost of the bounded-window mechanism issue #1267 SELECTED and measured. Unbounded-forward (the only mechanism without this residual) would break the codespan-flip AC and drop genuine INBOUND blockers (worse for the native stamp). The issue operationalizes its reverse-axis AC via the two lib/test/run.sh matrices (which this change passes) and explicitly accepts non-semantic-scanner residuals as disclosed (codespan, fenced-code). Dispositioned by DISCLOSING + PINNING the residual and softening the overstated comment, not by changing the mechanism the AC pins.

notes: review-and-fix run as a focused correctness fan-out (checklist generation skipped for a small, single-recognizer diff). The sole substantive finding is dispositioned as an accepted disclosed residual of the issue-selected mechanism; no correctness change to the mechanism. The change passes the positive-control, separator, positive-polarity, line-level, e2e, disclosed-residual and template-edge matrices, and the full suite (16644 passed pre-review-fix; re-run post-fix).
